source.title: Mechanisms of Non-Monotonic Scaling in Vision Transformers

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses scaling assumptions and reports results on Vision Transformer representation geometry, but does not measure held-out cross-entropy scaling, power-law fits, extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.gate_note: The study analyzes pretrained ViT-S/16, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/16 on ImageNet, not language-model pretraining loss. Its geometry results are related to scaling but do not directly test any listed version; the NC2 results are recorded under fits_no_version. Other reported measurements, including token similarity, probes, information scrambling, hub centrality, and positional-encoding interventions, do not measure the behaviors named by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study analyses layer-wise representation geometry, probes and attention graphs of three pretrained ImageNet ViTs (S/B/L). It reports no held-out loss, power-law fit, extrapolation, compute allocation or controlled shape sweep. It invokes Kaplan et al. only rhetorically, as the 'scaling assumption' its non-monotonic geometry results question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Note that the authors' 'performance' refers mainly to NC2 geometry and probe-efficiency per layer. Their own final probe accuracies rise with size: S 78.8%, B 84.2%, L 85.5% (Tables 8-10). ViT-L also has the highest NC4 in Table 5. So the claim that larger models 'perform worse' concerns representation geometry and depth efficiency, not task accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The paper performs layer-wise representation, probing, information-flow, and attention-graph analyses of pretrained vision models rather than fitting language-model held-out-loss scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that reported scrambling thresholds depend on their normalization and setup; results are limited to the studied pretrained ViT variants and ImageNet setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-layer Neural Collapse NC2 is non-monotonic in model size. Table 3 gives S 3.420, B 1.679, L 4.173; Table 5 gives S 0.564, B 0.486, L 0.541, with no explanation of the difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In pretrained ImageNet ViTs, final-layer class-geometry quality (NC2) does not improve monotonically with model size.

record.problems: Only three ViT variants and one image-classification setting are studied; the authors describe their analyses as correlational and say they do not intervene in training. The paper reports conflicting NC2 values for the same models in Tables 3 and 5 without explaining the difference. These measurements do not establish language-model loss-scaling behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing directly on the listed versions were omitted. Other reported measurements are outside the versions' named outcomes.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss is measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
No fits on small runs and no prediction of larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep of parameter and token counts.
ViT-S/B/L differ in width, depth and parameter count together; parameters are never held fixed and loss is not measured.
Image models are used, but no power law in loss or error is fitted.
Final-layer probe accuracy is reported for only three off-the-shelf models. No scale-performance relationship is fitted or tested.
No comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not relevant to the loss-scaling versions. Two cautions for readers. First, the paper calls ViT-L's geometry the worst, but in Table 5 ViT-S has the highest NC2 (0.564 vs 0.541), so the ordering is inconsistent across tables. Second, the final-layer linear-probe accuracy rises monotonically with size (Tables 8-10). This is weakly consistent with ordinary scaling, but it is uncontrolled and covers only three models, so it is not recorded as a test of V6. The models are frozen, the analysis is correlational, and there is no training intervention.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No power-law fit on smaller runs or prediction of larger runs is reported.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or scaling of optimal parameter and token counts is measured.
The paper compares different ViT sizes/depths, but does not hold parameter count fixed while varying architecture, nor measure loss.
The study uses image models but does not test whether held-out loss follows a power law in another modality or training regime.
ImageNet probe and classifier measurements are reported, but the study does not test downstream-task predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law exponents, fitting choices, or compute-optimal allocations is conducted.
